Server Atlas/Project & privacy
Open about the details

A small project.
A clear direction.

Server Atlas makes the path from searching to playing together shorter. Here is the current release, its sources and its data behavior.

The project

An independent community project developed for shuab. The native Horizon 2.2.0 package is MIT licensed, includes its Rust sources and targets Minecraft Java 26.3. Tested on Windows x64. No separate host patch or companion program is required.

Release and development

Public beta: 96 automated checks passed per loader. Some installation and gameplay combinations remain unverified. Horizon: 44 Rust tests; pinned native build.

Where the addresses come from

The dated catalog combines 488 previously researched addresses with 2,347 additional unique public Java addresses from Modrinth, for 2,835 total. Serverify's public documentation identified the additional source; this is an independent API integration.

Discovery in the mod

minecraftserve.rs and Modrinth have separate five-minute caches and a persistent limit of one public request per source per minute. Search text, personal servers, notes and player names are not sent to the directory APIs. Existing explicit Off remains Off. Normal status checks contact servers directly.

Website data

Search and filters run in your browser. A shareable search may appear in the URL and hosting request logs. The site's own code has no analytics, advertising scripts or external fonts. Clipboard access is used when you choose Copy address.

Images and product names

All product images are unedited captures of the built mod. Example profiles contain invented personal servers and notes; the discovery image is a real online test. Minecraft, Horizon and modloader names belong to their respective owners. The Server Atlas compass icon is original AI-generated artwork, exported for the platform icons. Product screenshots are real game captures.
